children: Installing an elevator is a major decision for any building owner. Whether it is a residential property, commercial space, or industrial building, adding a lift improves accessibility, convenience, and property value. However, the process involves careful planning, technical understanding, and the right service provider.

When considering such an important investment, companies like BG Elevators play a key role in guiding customers through the entire process. With proper knowledge and the right approach, you can ensure a smooth and successful installation experience with BG Elevators.
Why Installing an Elevator is Important
An elevator is no longer a luxury—it has become a necessity in modern buildings. With increasing urbanization and multi-storey constructions, lifts are essential for ease of movement.
Improved accessibility for elderly and disabled individuals
Before proceeding, it is important to understand all aspects of installation to avoid costly mistakes.

Factors to Consider Before Installing an Elevator
Installing an elevator is not just about choosing a design. There are multiple factors that must be evaluated carefully.
The available space in your building determines the type of elevator you can install. Shaft size, pit depth, and overhead clearance must be measured accurately.
You need to decide how many people or how much weight the elevator should carry. This depends on the building usage.
The height of the building affects the type of elevator system required. High-rise buildings need advanced systems compared to low-rise structures.
Costs include installation, maintenance, electricity consumption, and future upgrades. Planning your budget in advance helps avoid unexpected expenses.

Questions You Should Ask Before Installation
Before finalizing the installation, it is important to clarify all doubts. Asking the right questions helps you avoid future problems.
What type of elevator is best for my building?
What is the total installation cost?
How long will the installation take?
These questions will help you make an informed decision.
The elevator installation process involves several steps. Knowing these steps helps you understand the timeline and requirements.
Engineers inspect the building and analyze space, structure, and requirements.
A customized design is prepared based on your needs and building layout.
Construction of the elevator shaft, pit, and machine room (if required).
Installation of elevator components such as rails, cabin, and control systems.
Thorough testing is done to ensure proper functioning and safety compliance.
After successful testing, the elevator is handed over for use.

How long does it take to install an elevator?
The installation time usually depends on the type of elevator and building structure. On average, it can take anywhere from 2 to 6 weeks, including civil work and final testing.
What is the minimum space required for an elevator?
The space required depends on the type and capacity of the lift. Compact home elevators need less space, while commercial elevators require a larger shaft and additional structural provisions.
Is it necessary to have a machine room for every elevator?
No, not all elevators require a machine room. Machine Room Less (MRL) elevators are designed to save space and are commonly used in modern buildings.
What are the maintenance requirements after installation?

Regular maintenance is essential for safety and smooth operation. This includes periodic inspections, servicing of mechanical parts, and checking safety systems. Opting for an AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract) is recommended.
How much does elevator installation cost?
The cost varies based on factors like type of elevator, number of floors, load capacity, and customization. Residential elevators are generally more affordable than commercial systems.

Installing an elevator is a long-term investment that requires careful planning, proper knowledge, and the right decisions. From choosing the right type to understanding costs and safety, every step plays a crucial role in ensuring success.
